# The auxiliary-attachment gate: a 〜て auxiliary that must come out inside one
# span, with the label word its ATTACHES_TO row promises.
#
# Written 2026-09-21, and the reason it exists is a measurement rather than a
# defect. **Of the 38 adjacent 〜て + auxiliary pairs in gold.jsonl, every one
# is annotated as two spans and none as one** -- 引きずって | いった, 沈みこんで |
# いく, 頬張って | いる. The corpus's short-unit policy is deliberate and the
# rest of the engine is scored against it, but it means an auxiliary-merge row
# loses `strict` by construction (two gold spans become one), leaves `tolerant`
# neutral at best (the merge is credited as coarsening, never rewarded), cannot
# touch the compound metric (which holds no auxiliaries) and moves entry top-1
# on a denominator the merge itself changes. Four commits shipped in this family
# -- てる/でる, ている/でいる, ていく/でいく and てくる/ておく/てみる -- and the
# last two produced no positive cell anywhere in `score` while the corpus rate
# for their class went from 73.3% split to 1.6%.
#
# So this file is the cell those changes did not have. It is the mirror of
# spurious_merges.txt: that one refuses merges the engine must not make, this
# one requires merges it must. A row here is a claim the four commits above
# already made in their own tests and comments; what is new is that removing an
# ATTACHES_TO row now fails a test instead of improving a number.
#
# Columns, tab-separated: surface, label word, gold source.
#   surface  - the verb and its auxiliary, exactly as they appear in that gold
#              sentence. The test finds it in the sentence rather than parsing
#              it alone, because a bare surface is a different measurement --
#              spurious_merges.txt was ignored for four releases over exactly
#              that mistake (2026-09-16: 4 of its 26 "failures" were the test
#              parsing two-character surfaces out of context).
#   label    - one word that must appear in the winning entry's `conjugation`.
#              Not the whole label: 刻まれていた is "Passive/Potential
#              Progressive Past" and pinning every word would make this file a
#              second conjugation_labels.txt, which already exists and is
#              authoritative for that question. What this column pins is that
#              the auxiliary was recognised as itself.
#   source   - the gold sentence, by its `source` field. The test asserts gold
#              puts a boundary inside the surface, so a row that stopped
#              disagreeing with gold fails loudly rather than passing empty.
#
# Rows are every pair in gold.jsonl whose auxiliary this engine models, and a
# surface is the auxiliary's own span rather than the whole predicate. The
# difference is not cosmetic: 当惑 | していた and 行き | あっていました both split
# at a *different* boundary -- a noun+する and a compound verb -- and a row that
# spanned it would fail for a reason this file does not measure. The auxiliary
# is whole in both, which is the claim.
#
# Three pairs are deliberately absent.
#
# - して | おり (b:wn25517-3): おり is 居り and has no ATTACHES_TO row. Adding
#   one is a decision, not an omission.
# - 行って | きちゃえば: the gold span carries the ば. The merge is here under
#   the surface the engine actually produces, 行ってきちゃえ, which is the
#   longest chain in the file -- Approaching, Completive and an imperative in
#   one span.
# - 従って | いた (a:003521-2): **a defect, and an instructive one.** The engine
#   reads 従っていたから as a single seven-character span glossed 従う
#   "Progressive Want-to" -- the から absorbed and re-lemmatised, which is the
#   clause-final-particle class the corpus work measured at ~237 occurrences per
#   10k on visual-novel dialogue. This is that class inside the gold corpus,
#   where it had not been seen before. It is byte-identical before and after the
#   rows this file gates, so it is neither caused nor fixed by them; a row for it
#   belongs here once the particle class is fixed, not before.
吹き出してきた	Approaching	c1:mim-54
近づいてくる	Approaching	c1:mim-01
行ってきちゃえ	Approaching	c1:cas-16
引きずっていった	Directional	c1:mim-49
沈みこんでいく	Directional	c1:mim-45
折れていった	Directional	c1:mim-22
